title: Open a locker whose door a tipped case is leaning on, and take the case out upright
instruction: Take the blue case out of the locker and stand it upright on the green mat.
context: Things stowed in lockers, cupboards and overhead bins shift and lean on the door. The case holds a glass instrument and is marked this way up. Done by: flight attendants, stock clerks, care workers. The hazard is not stated. Unlike TK-F3WL2S and TK-GAUQTC, the door itself is the hidden support of a load that must be held through the gap.
setup: Distances in cm: x forward from the line between the arm bases, y to the robot's left of the midpoint between them; heights above the table top. Locker (fixed, grey painted steel, 10 mm walls): floor plate 1 cm thick, x 36 to 47, y -11 to 15; back wall x 46 to 47; side walls x 35.2 to 47 at y -11 to -10 and 14 to 15; roof x 35.2 to 47, y -11 to 15, 17.5 to 18.5 high. Inside: x 36 to 46, y -10 to 14, floor 1.0, roof 17.5 high. Door (pale yellow painted steel, 150 g): 8 mm thick, 23.6 wide, 16.1 tall (1.2 to 17.3 high), shut in the opening (x 35.2 to 36.0), hinged on a vertical axis at its right edge (x 35.6, y -10). It swings toward the robot, freely and damped, to 94 degrees; a magnetic catch holds it shut until it is pulled 3 degrees open. Handle: black bar 1.2 across and 6 tall, vertical, centred 10 high, 4 cm from the hinge (y -6), 4 cm in front of the door on two 8 mm standoffs. Case (loose, blue hard plastic, 150 g, marked this way up; it holds a glass instrument): 2.5 front to back, 11 wide, 16 tall, on end, its sides from y -6 to 5. The front edge of its base is on the floor 3.5 behind the door (x 39.5). It is tipped forward 12.5 degrees about that edge, its top resting on the inside of the shut door (it tips past its base at 9 degrees). Mat (fixed, green rubber, 2 mm): 14 x 14, centre x 18, y 8. Nothing else on the table. The case cannot be seen until the door opens.
scoring: Lean is the angle of the case's long edges from vertical. Tipped: at any time in the trial the case leaned more than 45 degrees (see the video); it is marked this way up, so laying it down counts too. Standing: lean at most 5 degrees, its lowest corner within 1.5 mm of the surface under it, still. 1.0: the case was never tipped and stands with its whole footprint on the green mat. 0.5: never tipped, and it stands outside the locker (wholly in front of the door's shut position) on the table, or partly on the mat. 0 otherwise: tipped at any time (even if later stood up), still in the locker, lying or leaning, held up off a surface, or moving. The trial ends at 1.0 once the 1.0 condition has held for 1 s; otherwise it scores the condition at the last step.
reset_notes: Shut the door against its catch and stand the case on end 3.5 cm behind the door, 4 cm from the hinge side, then tip its top forward onto the door. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Approximate. Parts are rigid boxes and cylinders. The task-file format places loose objects upright, so the start pose is set at reset. The catch is a spring preload in the door's first 3 degrees; past it the door turns freely, damped. Friction and masses are the simulator's values. The simulator cannot tell a held case from a released one. The layout is fixed, so a memorised replay of the demo cannot be ruled out.
